Custom CNC machining in Hangzhou, China.Prototypes and small production batches from drawings or samples, with orders starting at 1 piece.
Workshop visit and part discussion · January 2025 company archive.
Inside our machining workshop in Hangzhou.

LZZ is an ISO 9001-certified CNC machining company. We mill and turn custom components, using multi-axis machining where the geometry requires it. Dimensional inspection follows the agreed drawing requirements.
LZZ began making precision CNC machined parts for domestic equipment manufacturers.
We added CNC milling and turning equipment, along with multi-axis machines, to take on a wider range of industrial parts.
First-article checks became part of the workflow, alongside inspection during production and before shipment.
CMM, height gauges and optical projectors allowed us to inspect more complex custom components.
We expanded our OEM/ODM machining services to customers in Asia, North America and Europe.
We manufacture custom parts for a range of industries. Send your drawing, intended use and applicable standards so we can review the requirements for your project.

blocks.text: Machining for angled features and curved surfaces. We assess the geometry and tool access from your model.
Angled features may be reached by indexed positioning; continuous contours may need a simultaneous tool path. We review the model before choosing the machining route.
Five-axis machining provides angled tool access for deep cavities and continuous curves. Examples include impellers, curved components and multi-sided housings.

We review clamping areas, tool reach and clearance across the required orientations. Mark protected surfaces and features that must share a setup. Use the checklist below to send the model and dimensions for a size review.
Material options include aluminum, titanium, Inconel and hardened stainless steel. Specify the grade and condition, then define the finish and any surfaces where tool marks matter.
Will your part fit the setup?

Send the finished part and stock dimensions, including their weights. Mark clamping areas, protected surfaces and the clearance needed around the part. We need the model, drawing, material and quantity to review a suitable setup; machine travel, load limits and maximum part size are not listed here.
Indexed 3+2 positioning presents an angled face to the tool, then cuts with the rotary axes held in position.
Simultaneous five-axis motion changes tool orientation during the cut for suitable continuous contours. We review the model to select the machining method.
We review workholding and stock size, then check tool reach and inspection access. The quotation states the agreed process, services and records.

A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence.

blocks.text: Planning CNC parts for prototypes and repeat orders

For a housing or shaft, the surfaces that meet other parts matter as much as the outside shape. For a mounting block, identify its locating surfaces. Mark surfaces that seal, slide or carry load too, so tolerances can be discussed in relation to their function.
Compare milled pockets and housings with turned shafts and fittings. Some designs need both operations; the geometry determines the process choice.

Give the datums and mating details for critical features, with their acceptance limits. A 3D model shows the shape but may leave fits or surface texture undefined. It may also omit edge conditions and measurement methods. Include a controlled 2D drawing when these requirements apply.

Tolerances need review against the specific drawing. The material and feature geometry affect the assessment, as do the setup and measurement method; a single tolerance cannot apply to every catalog part. Agree on inspection requirements and supporting records for your design.

State the exact alloy or plastic grade and any material-certificate requirement. For coated parts, specify the finish and whether critical dimensions apply before or after treatment. Mark areas that need masking, cosmetic faces and burr-sensitive edges.
The material and finish checklist covers these details. Catalog photographs show shapes and surfaces; they cannot establish a coating specification or provide material certification.

Explain the purpose of the prototype. The checks may concern assembly fit and access. Appearance or a functional test may also guide revision or approval; agree the required checks before machining. If the design changes, issue a revised drawing with the affected dimensions identified; an email description alone is not enough.

The prototype machining examples show trial parts. When requesting a quote, separate the trial quantity from expected repeat orders. Orders start at 1 piece. Production takes 7-14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing; transit is additional. Confirm price and inspection requirements for your project.

Use the approved drawing revision and confirm the material and finish. Agree on the inspection scope and packaging requirements before ordering. If you need a first-article report or material documents, confirm their format and availability. Sample approval does not cover a changed design or material.

For orders like the low-volume parts shown here, use the RFQ checklist to prepare your inquiry. Confirm the price and available capacity in the quotation, along with the arrival date and shipping responsibilities.

Check payment, inspection and delivery requirements before ordering.FAQ topicsQuotes & orderingPayment, samples & after-sales termsPreparing a quotationProcesses & specificationsInspection & deliveryMachining studies & resourcesMinimum orderFrom 1 pieceShare first-order and expected repeat quantities for separate quotes.Production7-14 business daysAfter drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional.To quoteDrawing and specificationsSend drawing revision, units, material, finish, quantity and destination.Quotes & orderingWhat is the minimum order quantity?Orders start at 1 piece. Record the confirmed production schedule and delivery arrangements in your quotation and order.Payment, samples & after-sales termsWhich payment terms should I confirm?Before accepting a quote or placing an order, ask LZZ to confirm the payment method and currency. Agree the payment stages and the amount due at each stage for that order.How are samples charged?Ask for the sample machining and setup charges before approving the work. Confirm the sample freight cost and whether any sample fee can be credited to a later order.Which after-sales terms apply to my parts?Agree the terms for the quoted part before ordering. Confirm any warranty period and start date, exclusions and the procedure for reporting a problem. Ask who covers rework or replacement, return freight and any agreed refund.How do I report a nonconforming part?Send the drawing revision and part or batch reference, then include the affected quantity, photographs and measurement details. LZZ reviews the discrepancy against the agreed acceptance criteria and agrees corrective action with you.Preparing a quotationWhat should I send for a quotation?Include these details in your RFQ:Drawing revision and unitsExact material grade and conditionFinish and surface treatmentFirst-order and expected repeat quantitiesDelivery destinationSTEP model, where availableDimensioned 2D drawing with critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirementsDoes the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing?No. The inquiry form prepares an email draft. Check the draft, open it in your email application, attach your drawings and send it there. Copy and download options are also available; preparing a draft does not send an inquiry to LZZ.Processes & specificationsWhich machining services can I discuss with LZZ?Our five service areas are CNC milling, CNC turning, five-axis CNC machining, plastic machining and casting machining. Share the complete part geometry for review of the machining route. We also review workholding and finishing requirements. For castings, agree who supplies and approves the blank.How should I specify the material and finish?Specify the exact material grade and condition. A broad label such as aluminum, steel or plastic leaves the grade undefined. Identify cosmetic faces and surface treatment requirements, then mark masked areas and dimensions to check after finishing. Record the agreed specification in the quotation.Can every feature hold ±0.01 mm?No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional engineering reference for selected critical features after review, not a general part tolerance or guarantee. Material and geometry affect the achievable limit, along with the setup and measurement method. Identify each critical feature on the drawing for confirmation.Inspection & deliveryWhich inspection documents should I request?Specify the dimensional results and first-article records you need before ordering. Include material traceability and finishing documents where required. Agree the features and sampling plan, then confirm the report format. For supplier qualification, request the current certificate for Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., including its number, issuer, validity, scope and verification details. Company awards are separate from the ISO certificate, and quality-system certification does not replace part-specific acceptance or industry approval.How are packing and international shipping agreed?Provide the destination, receiving requirements and any vulnerable or cosmetic surfaces that need protection. Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time.Machining studies & resourcesWhat do the machining studies show?Original LZZ workshop photographs show part features and machining setups. Ask for the sample machining and setup charges before approving the work. Confirm the sample freight cost and whether any sample fee can be credited to a later order.
Which after-sales terms apply to my parts?

Agree the terms for the quoted part before ordering. Confirm any warranty period and start date, exclusions and the procedure for reporting a problem. Ask who covers rework or replacement, return freight and any agreed refund.
How do I report a nonconforming part?

Send the drawing revision and part or batch reference, then include the affected quantity, photographs and measurement details. LZZ reviews the discrepancy against the agreed acceptance criteria and agrees corrective action with you.
What should I send for a quotation?
Include these details in your RFQ:
Dimensioned 2D drawing with critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirements
Does the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing?

No. The inquiry form prepares an email draft. Check the draft, open it in your email application, attach your drawings and send it there. Copy and download options are also available; preparing a draft does not send an inquiry to LZZ.
Which machining services can I discuss with LZZ?

Our five service areas are CNC milling, CNC turning, five-axis CNC machining, plastic machining and casting machining. Share the complete part geometry for review of the machining route. We also review workholding and finishing requirements. For castings, agree who supplies and approves the blank.
How should I specify the material and finish?

Specify the exact material grade and condition. A broad label such as aluminum, steel or plastic leaves the grade undefined. Identify cosmetic faces and surface treatment requirements, then mark masked areas and dimensions to check after finishing. Record the agreed specification in the quotation.

No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional engineering reference for selected critical features after review, not a general part tolerance or guarantee. Material and geometry affect the achievable limit, along with the setup and measurement method. Identify each critical feature on the drawing for confirmation.
Which inspection documents should I request?

Specify the dimensional results and first-article records you need before ordering. Include material traceability and finishing documents where required. Agree the features and sampling plan, then confirm the report format. The quotation records the included document package and any additional cost; request current calibration evidence separately where needed.

LZZ is ISO 9001 certified. For supplier qualification, request the current certificate for Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., including its number, issuer, validity, scope and verification details. Company awards are separate from the ISO certificate, and quality-system certification does not replace part-specific acceptance or industry approval.
How are packing and international shipping agreed?

Provide the destination, receiving requirements and any vulnerable or cosmetic surfaces that need protection. Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time.
What do the machining studies show?

Original LZZ workshop photographs show part features and machining setups. The studies use them to discuss the machining sequence and drawing requirements for a similar part. They contain no customer performance or inspection results and do not establish a delivery outcome.

blocks.text: Prepare the technical files and order details we need to quote your part.
3D model and 2D drawing when needed, part number, units and revision.
Exact material or functional requirement, finish details and applicable standards.
Critical dimensions, datums, tolerances and inspection requirements.
Initial quantity and expected repeat pattern.
Arrival date, packaging, shipping basis and relevant customs requirements.
Use this worksheet to record the drawing revision and critical features, along with document and shipping requirements. It contains no inspection results.

Include a 3D model, such as STEP, and a 2D drawing when dimensions, fits or surface requirements are not fully defined in the model. Label the part number and units, and identify the drawing revision. If the files disagree, identify which document controls before requesting a quotation.
For multi-axis parts, include the overall envelope, stock dimensions and part weight where known so tool access and setup can be reviewed.

If you have a sample without a drawing, describe the known requirements. Ask which measurements or design work are needed to define the part. A sample alone cannot establish hidden material or treatment requirements.
Mark the dimensions used for acceptance

Identify mating bores and shaft fits on the drawing, with their datums and tolerances. Mark sealing faces, threads and any other critical features too. State whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.

If you need a particular inspection record, send the format or an example with your inquiry. Agree the inspection and documentation requirements before ordering. Ask LZZ to confirm the measurement method and instrument range, then request calibration evidence and confirmation that your required project records are available.
Specify the material and final surface
State the exact alloy or polymer grade, or the functional requirement if selection is still open. Include any required material documentation and whether substitutes may be considered.

Provide the finish specification and appearance requirements. Mark cosmetic faces and masked areas, and define edge conditions. Include customer or industry standards and certificates required for this part or program, stating each standard, revision and scope.
A material or capability category on this site does not establish industry certification or application compliance. The material and finish checklist explains the decisions behind these fields.

Our quotation states the proposed process and material. It also sets out finishing, order quantity, inspection documents, production schedule and shipping basis. We clarify open geometry or acceptance requirements before you approve production.
